reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a front-running bot with guaranteed 10x profits and claims users can passively generate thousands per day. It directs viewers to deploy and fund a smart contract with BNB, activate automated trading, and says 90 percent of profits will return to their wallet. These unusually high-return claims paired with a concrete funding and execution flow support the interpretation of a deceptive financial solicitation, though the contract's behavior, fund destination, and actual returns are not verified.

citations.quote: Pancakeswap front run bot (NO DOWNLOADS) - guaranteed 10x profits easy profits
The new minimum ammount needed for the bot to work properly is now 0.4 BNB due to higher transaction fees.
Bots immediately buy milliseconds before the confirmation of liquidity - Then sell seconds after for guaranteed profit
we're going to deploy this to our wallet
the next step in this process is just funding your contract

opening.argument: The presentation includes an explicit, material risk warning rather than portraying participation as risk-free: it says using less than the stated minimum "will just burn your funds" and requires Mainnet. That warning is concrete, operationally relevant, and tells viewers that loss is possible if they follow the setup incorrectly. The return language should therefore be read alongside a stated funding risk and network requirement, not as an unconditional promise that every viewer will profit. The material also describes a technical process whose outcome depends on liquidity and transaction conditions, making the warning relevant to how a careful viewer would evaluate the claims.

citations.quote: Lower than 0.4 BNB will just burn your funds. Also you have to be on Mainnet or this won't work.
it will transact uh the Liquidity as soon as is added to a token

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and promotional language are certainly aggressive, but they do not erase the plainly stated warning that an insufficient amount can burn funds. The prosecution also treats the 0.4 BNB requirement as proof of deceptive solicitation, although the same statement expressly presents it as a condition for the bot to work and warns of a specific loss consequence. The evidence supports a risky technical claim, but does not establish that the creator concealed risk or promised every user a guaranteed outcome.

citations.quote: guaranteed 10x profits easy profits
Lower than 0.4 BNB will just burn your funds. Also you have to be on Mainnet or this won't work.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning that an incorrectly sized deposit may burn funds does not make the broader offer non-deceptive. The same material labels profits guaranteed and says the bot can generate thousands per day. A technical condition and a loss warning can coexist with a misleading promise of returns; neither establishes that the contract actually works or that the advertised profits are attainable.

citations.quote: guaranteed 10x profits easy profits
you will be able to passively generate thousands a day

opening.argument: The video's observable center is an operational programming demonstration: it creates a Solidity file, compiles it in Remix, connects injected Web3, deploys a contract, and shows how the action function is used. The speaker explains contract addresses, the wrapped BNB token, the PancakeSwap router, and the deployment workflow. That is consistent with an educational technology tutorial or demonstration, even if the presenter also discusses expected performance. Showing a procedure and describing the presenter's experience does not by itself prove that viewers were being deceived or that the code had a hidden malicious function.

citations.quote: going to create a new contract
So, we go to version 66. Solidity. And that's it. Let me. Go compile
so we're gonna do injected web 3
The action button then engages all the constructors that I built in

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that a tutorial demonstrates deployment does not determine its classification. Its instructional steps are aimed at putting BNB into the demonstrated contract and activating automated trades. The presenter also describes unusually large returns and a mechanism that allegedly sends profits back to the wallet. Thus, the technical format is not a neutral coding lesson; it is the means by which the claimed financial opportunity is presented.

citations.quote: the next step in this process is just funding your contract
it automatically buys and sells for you
it's already around 15x

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The deployment walkthrough is not merely abstract education: it directs viewers to fund the deployed contract and press the action control. The claimed demonstration of returns is also presented as a successful result, while the evidence does not independently verify the contract's behavior, the displayed result, or the asserted profits. Technical detail can make a financial solicitation more credible without making its claims reliable.

citations.quote: For sake of this video, I will do 0.2 BNB. Might as well make it 0.4.
we will just go over here and press the action button
it's already around 15x

opening.argument: The material can also be understood as promotion of a software-based service or tool for automated trading, rather than proof of a conventional scam mechanism. It provides setup resources and explains the claimed function of a contract interacting with PancakeSwap. Crucially, the supplied material does not show a request for a password, private key, or account credentials, nor does it describe recruiting a downline or paying referral commissions. It says funds are sent to the user's deployed contract and describes a claimed automated process, but that alone does not establish that the creator secretly receives the funds or controls the viewer's wallet.

citations.quote: In this video I am showcasing how to run and deploy a LEAKED $15000 Front Running bot written with Solidity.
we're gonna send some funds to that contract
90% will automatically trans back to your wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a software tool does not make the financial mechanism ordinary commerce. The instructions require viewers to fund a contract, activate it, and rely on promised returns. The prosecution need not prove a password request or referral scheme when the alleged mechanism is a funded contract offering automated profits. The absence of those other mechanisms is therefore not exculpatory.

citations.quote: the next step in this process is just funding your contract
The action button then engages all the constructors that I built in
Then sell seconds after for guaranteed profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam need not request credentials, recruit a downline, or use commissions. Here, the material solicits a substantial BNB transfer into a contract while asserting guaranteed profit and massive daily earnings. It does not establish that viewers retain control of the funds, that the contract performs the claimed trades, or that the advertised return is genuine; saying money should return to a wallet is only an assertion.
